audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Quinn levels 3, first item and 2+ items and Skill at 4-5 and 6; the packet chart is Skill, Quinn, Skill, Cho'Gath, Cho'Gath, Cho'Gath, Cho'Gath.
audit.why: The mirror slice already committed Cho'Gath's page to the packet chart as one atomic group, so this side has to match or mirror-fix.js overwrites it.
audit.corrected: win[2..6] and phases[2..6].side re-cut, ratings inverted, and whys[3], [4], [5] rewritten so the prose no longer claims Quinn wins those stages.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was described as Quinn's roam spike; the first-item row as Quinn's lethality spike.
audit.why: Feast arrives at 6 on an 80s cooldown as true damage, and every takedown is permanent max health — that is the spike that ends Quinn's window.
audit.corrected: whys[4], whys[5], spikes[1].text and spikes[2].text rewritten around Feast and his first health item.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never mentioned the silence, and told the player to 'blind his Q on cooldown so he can't engage'.
audit.why: Feral Scream silences (11/10.5/10/9.5/9) — silenced, Vault will not cast at all, so the escape is gone; that is the interaction that kills Quinn here. Blinding Assault hinders vision, so it does nothing to Rupture, but Vorpal Spikes releases from his attacks, so the blind DOES deny that. Rupture knocks up, and Behind Enemy Lines is a channel, so a Rupture cancels it.
audit.corrected: report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[1].d, wants.foe[0] and mid rewritten to state all three.

audit.why: Feral Scream 11s at rank 1, Rupture 6s, Vorpal Spikes 8 to 4, Feast 80/70/60.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Feast's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Vorpal Spikes and an 11s Feral Scream turn every step-up into a trade he wins — silenced, you cannot even Vault out.

edits.before: Behind Enemy Lines exports your lead — roam on every shove. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Cho'Gath's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Feast lands at 6: 80s, true damage, and every takedown is permanent max health. Shove and roam instead of trading.

edits.before: You out-trade a stack-less Cho — blind his Q, bait the knockup, and take plates while he can't engage.
edits.after: Vorpal Spikes and an 11s Feral Scream silence flip the trade — silenced, Vault will not cast and you cannot leave.

edits.before: R turns your shove into roam pressure; snowball mid/bot before his Feast HP ever comes online.
edits.after: Feast lands at 6: true damage on an 80s cooldown, and every stack is permanent max health.

edits.before: Your lethality/crit spike plus blind still beat a one-item Cho — force the lane and bank kills before he walls up.
edits.after: One health item on top of Feast stacks and your lethality stops mattering — take the plates, not the fight.

edits.before: R lets you roam mid/bot the instant Cho recalls or shoves — turn your lane lead into a 9/0 game before Feast stacks matter.
edits.after: Feast at 6 is true damage on an 80s cooldown and every kill is permanent max health — never trade down low into it.

edits.before: Your lethality/crit spike plus blind keep you ahead, but bank the kills now — this is the last window before Feast HP makes your autos chip damage.
edits.after: Bank your kills before his first health item: Feast stacks plus HP turn your lethality autos into chip, and the blind does nothing to his abilities.

edits.before: This is your lane. With your first lethality components, blind his Q on cooldown so he can't engage, and bait the Rupture before you step up. At 6 your real power is R — the moment you shove, scout and roam, because every kill you bank now is a kill you steal before his Feast HP makes you irrelevant. Stack plates, shove, leave.
edits.after: This is your lane through level 3. Bait Rupture before you step up, and note the blind only touches his autos — still worth it, since Vorpal Spikes rides those autos. At 6 Feast arrives and the lane stops being yours: shove, scout, roam. Every kill you bank now is one you steal before his Feast HP makes you irrelevant. Stack plates, shove, leave.

edits.before: Land Q (Rupture) knockup then W (Feral Scream) silence to lock you in for a full combo
edits.after: Rupture your channel: the knockup cancels Behind Enemy Lines and sets up Feral Scream

edits.before: Track Cho'Gath's Feast: True-damage execute. Don’t sit low. When it is down — Vault-blind + R him.
edits.after: Feral Scream silences for 11s at rank 1 — silenced, Vault will not cast. Your blind does kill Vorpal Spikes.

edits.before: - Cho'Gath Feast: matchup-defining — True-damage execute. Don’t sit low. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Feral Scream: 11s at rank 1 — silenced, Vault will not cast at all. - Rupture: 6s knockup, and it cancels Behind Enemy Lines. - Vorpal Spikes rides his autos, so your blind denies it. - Feast: 80s of true damage.

edits.before: True-damage execute. Don’t sit low. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Feast is 80s of true damage — never trade down into it, and never sit low.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Feral Scream's silence means Vault will not cast — you cannot leave.

notes: Rupture carries a derived 'grounding' flag Riot's description does not support (knockup, damage, slow), so no grounding claim was written — the knockup and the silence are enough. The early/mid/late blocks are first-person ('you'/'I' mixed); mid is converted here, early and late still want a voice pass, which the mirror auditor also flagged.
